items.title: AI-stock sell-off sends the S&P 500 down 4.4%, its worst day since April 2025
items.summary: On Thursday 5 November the S&P 500 fell 4.4%, the Dow 3.4% and the Nasdaq composite 5.5%, led by companies tied to AI data-centre spending. Every S&P 500 sector fell.
items.why: A shock day for US stocks: it pushed volatility up and is why the market regime reads Unstable.

items.title: A brutal sell-off for AI stocks sends Wall Street reeling, and the S&P 500 tumbles 4.4%
items.summary: The Dow dropped more than 1,800 points and the Nasdaq composite fell 5.5%.
items.why: Second copy of the same agency story on another site.

items.title: Nasdaq has its steepest weekly fall in 19 months after the US midterms; Tesla lost 10.8% on Thursday
items.summary: A week-in-review says about $3 trillion of market value was erased on 5 November as investors weighed tighter AI regulation after Democrats won both chambers of Congress. Nvidia fell 9.3% and Tesla 10.8% that day; both bounced about 5% on Friday.
items.why: Explains the size of last week's moves in the watchlist's largest stocks.

items.title: Nvidia falls as its board opens an independent investigation; wider market rallies
items.summary: Reports say Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation involving its chief executive over the weekend. The shares opened about 8% lower on Monday 9 November while the S&P 500 rose.
items.why: Company-specific risk in the index's largest stock, with earnings due on 17 November. Not yet backed by a company filing seen in this run.

items.title: Markets price a high chance of a December Fed rate rise after strong US jobs data
items.summary: After a stronger-than-expected October jobs report, traders put the odds of a December rate rise at about 80%, which capped gold's gains.
items.why: Rate expectations drive bonds, the dollar and gold; US CPI this week is the next test.

items.title: Gold rises to a two-week high above $4,100 as oil falls and the dollar weakens
items.summary: Gold and silver extended their recovery on 9 November as lower oil prices eased inflation worries. China's central bank bought 25.8 tonnes of gold in October, its largest monthly addition in three years.
items.why: Runs against the app's bearish trend reading on gold and silver.

items.title: Oil drops on hopes of US-Iran de-escalation; Brent down from $112 at the start of November
items.summary: Brent crude fell about 4% to roughly $94 on 9 November on hopes of diplomatic progress between Washington and Tehran.
items.why: Headline-driven: oil can gap either way on news from the Gulf, straight through chart levels.

items.title: Bitcoin below $75,000 as spot ETF outflows continue
items.summary: Bitcoin stayed under $75,000 on 9 November with a rebound proving elusive; JPMorgan estimated $431 million left spot bitcoin ETFs the previous Thursday. Ether was near $2,108.
items.why: Fund outflows are steady selling pressure and fit the bearish scores on all four coins.

items.title: Dollar slides to a one-month low after the US midterms as oil and Treasury yields fall
items.summary: The dollar fell after Democrats' midterm victory; the euro rose to about $1.126 and the 10-year Treasury yield dropped to 4.85%, its lowest since 10 September.
items.why: Runs against the app's bearish trend reading on EUR/USD and Treasury futures.

items.title: Dollar firms on safe-haven demand after the AI sell-off, though lower yields cap gains
items.summary: On 6 November the dollar index rose 0.25% to 101.76 and the euro slipped to about $1.12 ahead of the US payrolls report.
items.why: Shows the dollar's direction changing day to day: a choppy backdrop for FX trend setups.
